gappers.catalyst: No CRWV-specific news since a Nov 23 conference notice; the move is the AI/neocloud complex repricing for a second straight session.
gappers.catalyst_detail: Still no company-specific release: the newest CRWV item is a Nov 23 conference-participation notice, and the last substantive one is Q3 results on Nov 10. What is driving it is a second consecutive session of AI-infrastructure de-rating. NVDA fell 5% pre-market on top of Tuesday's 6% slump, with criticism now aimed at US-government influence over the company's governance following Jensen Huang's return as CEO. Broadcom, AMD, Micron and Intel are down up to 7%, and TradingEconomics describes an active 'unwind on speculative positions on AI'. CRWV's own Q3 is the bear case: revenue tripled to $3.661B and operating income reached $207M, but net loss widened to $709M because net interest expense hit $846M, with Q4 interest guided to $1.05-1.15B against $37-39B of planned capex.
gappers.why: A debt-funded, pre-profit buildout is a long-duration asset whose equity reprices first when risk appetite and the AI demand narrative crack together. Interest expense now runs roughly 4x operating income, financed with ~$4.2B of converts, a $2.6B facility and a program for up to 35M Class A shares, so the market is marking financing risk rather than the $132.5B backlog. Critically, the Nov 23 Huang-return headline that sparked a +28% bounce has now inverted into a governance negative, so the bounce's own catalyst is gone.
gappers.impact: Continuation of a confirmed downtrend. $39.71 sits only 1.1% above the Nov 20 52-week low of $39.28 and 69.2% below the 52-week high of $138.25; the +28% Nov 23 bounce has now fully retraced. The dissonance worth flagging is volume: Nov 24 traded 61.5M against a 20-day average of 71.3M, a ratio of 0.86 - below average. Across all seven qualifying gappers the Nov 24 volume ratio ranges 0.49-0.97, so this entire complex is grinding to new lows WITHOUT capitulation volume, which argues the de-rating is not finished rather than that it is exhausted. Sector read-through is total: NBIS, BE, ONDS, AMKR, KLIC and ORCL are all down 5-6.8% with no company news of their own.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: Factor-driven with no durable thesis; the interest-expense overhang is a multi-quarter problem, not a days-to-weeks catalyst, and the rulebook's late-cycle read does not favour Technology.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace - 0 positions, 100% cash, 0/3 weekly trades. The gate fails on arithmetic: at ATR14 of 16.92% of price, the mandatory 10% trailing stop sits just 0.59 ATR below spot, well inside a single day's range, and the +20% level needed for 2:1 is only 1.18 ATR away. Price is 51.3% below its 200-SMA, failing the long filter independently. Cannot clear 2:1 at any stop distance compatible with the 10% rule. Research only - no order.

gappers.catalyst_detail: No company news since the Nov 12 Q3 report, which itself closed -16.84%. The only fresh single-name items remain price-target cuts - Truist to $245 on Nov 21, Baird to $200 on Nov 23 - both still far above spot, i.e. the sell-side chasing price down rather than leading it. Q3 frames the risk: revenue rose 571% y/y to $980.8M with adjusted EBITDA of $465.8M and positive operating income of $50.4M, but non-current debt went from $4.103B to $14.003B, quarterly capex reached $7.300B, and operating cash flow was a $273.0M outflow. The $3.5B Citi facility signed Oct 22 is 364-day paper at SOFR +2.75% stepping up to 3.50%.
gappers.why: The same funding-structure mechanism as CRWV, not a demand story: short-dated floating-rate debt financing a long-dated buildout. With VIX at 30.87 and the 10-year at a two-week low, the market reprices refinancing risk on 364-day paper and the equity absorbs it - which is why NBIS falls despite >$40B of disclosed long-term contracts and 571% growth. Its high beta does the rest.
gappers.impact: Reads as drift rather than liquidation, and the volume supports that: Nov 24 did 28.7M against a 32.3M 20-day average, a 0.89 ratio. At $81.71 it is 11.1% above the Nov 20 low of $73.52 - the largest cushion of the four high-volatility names - but 70.9% below the Nov 11 high of $299.86. The Nov 20 low is the level that matters and it has not been retested yet today. Chart shape is identical to the rest of the cohort, which is the point: nothing here is idiosyncratic.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: Factor- and funding-driven; nothing structural has changed since Nov 12 and the only two analyst actions in hand are target cuts.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace - 0 positions, 0/3 weekly. gappers.catalyst: No negative company news at all; giving back the Nov 23 Huang-return spike as that catalyst inverts into an NVDA governance negative.
gappers.catalyst_detail: No negative company news whatsoever - the last release is a Nov 20 community donation, and the fundamental record is the strongest on the board: Q3 revenue of $1,235.8M (+138.1% y/y), product revenue +179.4%, GAAP gross margin 33.8%, operating income $225.4M against $7.8M a year earlier, net income $250.3M, diluted EPS $0.78, FY26 guidance raised to $4.4-4.6B revenue and $3.10-3.40 non-GAAP EPS, cash of $2.487B, and S&P 500 inclusion. Commercially it holds a 900MW onsite-power agreement with NTT DATA - its largest international project - plus Oracle's stated intent for up to 2.8GW. What is actually happening is the Nov 23 Huang-return spike, worth +21% to +27% in a session, being handed back over Nov 24-25 as that same headline turns into a governance criticism of NVDA.
gappers.why: A valuation and duration unwind, not an earnings problem. At $146.40 against $3.10-3.40 of FY26 non-GAAP EPS the stock trades at roughly 43-47x forward, and essentially all of the NTT DATA 900MW revenue ships from 2027. A multiple that high resting on 2027+ cash flows is the most rate- and sentiment-sensitive cohort in the market, so with the Nasdaq 100 down 12.9% on the month, VIX above 30 and tariffs pending, the multiple compresses regardless of the last print. The Huang headline inflated it on no fundamental change; the reversal of that headline deflates it.
gappers.impact: Continued mean-reversion of a sentiment spike rather than a fundamental break, and volume agrees: Nov 24 did 13.7M against a 17.9M average, a 0.77 ratio - the second-lightest participation on the board. $146.40 is 106.6% above its 52-week low of $75.70, by far the most air beneath it of any name here, and 55.5% below the Nov high of $351.28. Of the whole cohort BE has given back the least relative to its base. Read-through runs both ways: BE's own Nov 12 sector release bundled GEV/CEG/TLN/PWR, and TLN is the name carrying the dated $349-356 limit plan from the Nov 18-20 handoff.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: The gap is the unwind of a two-day sentiment spike whose catalyst has now inverted; the NTT/Oracle contracts are genuinely structural but 2027-dated, too far out to support a swing entry into a falling tape.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace - 0 positions, 0/3 weekly, and every name ranked above it fails the same gate, so it crowds out nothing. It fails anyway: ATR14 at 14.83% of price puts the 10% trailing stop 0.67 ATR below spot, inside one day's range, and price is 30.2% below its 200-SMA - the shallowest breach on the board but still a clear fail. Carry it forward as the first candidate to revisit if the operator ever approves an ATR-based stop in place of the fixed 10%: real and accelerating fundamentals, the mildest drawdown, and the largest 52-week-low cushion. Research only - no order.

gappers.catalyst_detail: No company-specific news since Nov 20, when Ondas co-hosted a defense technology summit with Palantir and Regna AI - an item that still closed -11.11%. The Nov 18 Aston Martin F1 multi-year partnership closed +0.68%. The relevant record is the Nov 12 Q3: revenue hit a record $167.5M versus $10.1M a year earlier with bookings of $214M and backlog of $835M, FY26 guidance was raised to at least $550M and 2027 to at least $1.1B, and adjusted-EBITDA profitability was pulled forward a quarter to Q3 2027 - yet the stock closed -7.16% on it. The reason sits in the same release: gross margin collapsed to 21.8% from 43.1% sequentially, operating loss widened to $189.5M and net loss was $64.7M, against $820.3M of cash after six completed acquisitions.
gappers.why: The market is refusing to pay for acquired, low-margin revenue growth. Ondas has bought six companies and booked record top-line, but margin halved sequentially and the operating loss is larger than the quarter's entire revenue - so the growth is being read as consolidation accounting rather than earning power, with adjusted-EBITDA breakeven still three quarters out. Every single positive release since Oct 29 has closed red (-8.14%, -8.98%, -14.23%, -6.70%, -7.16%, -11.11%), which is the signature of persistent distribution into good news. Layered on top, the broad risk-off tape is hitting the speculative small-cap defense/drone complex hardest.
gappers.impact: The most negative technical read on the board, and the one genuinely new development since the 07:09 ET run: at $3.66 ONDS is 1.9% BELOW its prior 52-week low of $3.73, so it is making a new low rather than testing one. It is 74.5% off the 52-week high of $15.28 and 54.2% below its 200-SMA. Volume is the one near-confirming print in the cohort - Nov 24 did 45.7M against a 47.2M average, a 0.97 ratio, essentially full participation, versus 0.49-0.89 for the rest. A new low on near-average volume with no company news is distribution, not a headline spike that mean-reverts. Read-through to the drone/defense peers is visible in the same scan: UMAC -5.19%, RCAT -3.66%, DPRO -3.06%, KTOS -2.52%, AVAV -2.29%.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: Breaking to a new 52-week low on full volume with no catalyst and a sequential margin collapse; the backlog is real but the structural case needs an inflection in margin, not in bookings, and that is three quarters out.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace - 0 positions, 0/3 weekly. gappers.catalyst_detail: Nothing company-specific. The newest release is a Nov 18 dividend increase from $0.08352 to $0.08436 - under a tenth of a cent - and the only analyst action in the window is B. Riley trimming its target to $38 from $41 on Nov 9. The move is transmitted from the semis complex: Broadcom, AMD, Micron and Intel are down up to 7% pre-market after Nov 24's MU -11% / AMD -8.9% / INTC -8.1% / NVDA -5.86%, and Ambarella guided Q4 revenue to $70-75M against roughly $112M consensus, falling 37% after Tuesday's close. Layered on is the pending US tariff announcement on China, the EU and 14 other economies, which lands directly on AMKR's Korea/Asia-heavy footprint. AMKR closed Nov 24 down 8.62% at $31.81.
gappers.why: AMKR is the highest-beta transmission line in the group at beta 2.43 and the purest OSAT read on AI advanced-packaging demand, so any demand-side datapoint in accelerated computing hits it amplified. Ambarella's guide and the Nov 24 memory/logic selloff speak to exactly the packaging volumes AMKR is building $12B of Arizona capacity against; tariffs compound it by threatening the cost base of its Asian footprint. The market is discounting the forward volume assumption, not the delivered quarter.
gappers.impact: Thin-book quote rather than distribution, but now at a new low. Nov 24 traded 2.84M against a 4.97M 20-day average - a 0.57 ratio, the lightest participation of any deep-dive name - and at $29.94 the stock is a fraction below its $29.95 52-week low set Nov 20, so it joins ONDS in making a new low this morning. A marginal new low on the lightest volume in the cohort is the weakest possible confirmation, which cuts both ways: it is the most likely of the five to snap back, and also the one where the low means least. The valuation dissonance is the real story: forward P/E 12.18, trailing 12.82, Q3 net income $191M on $1.991B revenue, 18.3% gross margin, $2.4B cash against $2.5B debt, and $3B of NVIDIA prepayment agreements across Arizona and South Korea - the cheapest fundamentals on the board sitting on a 67.1% drawdown.
gappers.horizon_reasoning: SHORT_TERM for the gap itself - an unconfirmed thin-book move at a new low with no company catalyst - but carry AMKR forward as the single LONG_TERM watch candidate of the five: the NVIDIA prepayment contracts and 12x forward earnings are structural, and it is the only name here whose ATR sits inside the rulebook's viable band.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Nothing to displace - 0 positions, 0/3 weekly.
